title: Stratos Payments - POC scoping: workload & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping call to define workload characteristics and success criteria for a 6-week POC. Discussed QPS/concurrency, input/output token distributions, target latencies, cost constraints, required benchmarks (latency, p95/p99, throughput), and timeline for pilot. Agreed to run two benchmark workloads: 1) low-latency auth/verification path and 2) high-throughput batch enrichment. Next steps: Redwood to share Dedicated sizing spreadsheet, security docs, and benchmark harness; Stratos to provide sample traffic traces and success criteria spreadsheet.
next_steps: Redwood -> Share Dedicated sizing + cost spreadsheet (Alex) by 2025-09-15
Stratos -> Upload 2 weeks of anonymized traffic traces and a sample of 500 production prompts by 2025-09-17
Schedule benchmark run and initial results review (target week of 2025-09-22) - Priya to coordinate
action_items: Alex Reed - Share Dedicated sizing spreadsheet, pricing tiers, and benchmark harness link - due 2025-09-15
Priya Sen - Prepare benchmark harness repo and runbook; propose 2 benchmark configs (latency-focused, throughput-focused) - due 2025-09-16
Mike Chen - Export and sanitize 2 weeks of production traffic (anonymize PII) and tokenized examples - due 2025-09-17
Laura Diaz - Confirm security contacts and send SOC2 + network requirements doc request - due 2025-09-16
transcript: 15:00 Alex Reed: hey everyone thanks for joining from both sides, um we wanted to keep this focused on the POC scoping for the Stratos payments flows, especially around throughput and latency 15:12 Mike Chen: yeah thanks Alex, excited to dig in; goal is to validate that Redwood can meet our auth latency and also scale for batch enrichment, we tested some models in-house and we're hitting cost and latency tradeoffs 15:30 Priya Sen: cool, quick intros? I'm Priya, solutions engineer at Redwood, I lead perf/benchmarks; Alex will own the commercial side 15:38 Laura Diaz: Laura here - head of platform; Jamal is our SRE, Kayla is PM for the payments product 15:45 Jamal Ortiz: hey all, will be focused on runbook and infra constraints, we run on GCP in us-west2, private VPC peering preferred 15:58 Alex Reed: perfect - agenda is: define success criteria, walk through traffic patterns (qps/concurrency/token lengths), pick benchmark configs, and agree on timeline 16:05 Mike Chen: to give context, our product has two main LLM touchpoints: 1) real-time auth/verification ~ decisioning after login - this is low-latency, ~120-200ms target but currently acceptable is up to 400ms; traffic ~50 qps peak with spikes to 100 qps for 30-60s during batch logins. 16:22 Kayla Park: second path is post-transaction enrichment where we augment ledger entries with risk signals and merchant descriptors. This is batchy, can be async. Throughput goal is 300-500 qps sustained during nightly windows, latency per request can be higher (1-2s) 16:39 Priya Sen: good split. When you say qps are those per-tenant or cross-tenant? 16:44 Mike Chen: those are cross-tenant totals; single tenant peak tends to be 10-20 qps 16:52 Alex Reed: can you describe concurrency shape? i.e., average concurrent open sessions hitting Redwood per second and typical request fanout (multiple calls per user) 16:58 Mike Chen: mostly single-call per user for auth. For enrichment, we fanout - a transaction can spawn 3-4 model calls for scoring, metadata, and normalization. So concurrent model invocations maybe 1.5x the user qps on average 17:15 Priya Sen: noted. Token distribution? what's typical input length and expected generated tokens? 17:22 Kayla Park: auth prompts are small, 30-80 input tokens, expect 10-50 output tokens (usually single-line decisions). Enrichment prompts are larger: 200-800 input tokens (full transaction context + merchant history), outputs are 50-300 tokens 17:38 Jamal Ortiz: also note we sometimes include PDF text snippets for chargebacks - those are very large, but we plan to pre-extract and summarize locally before sending to model 17:50 Priya Sen: ok that helps. For modeling cost and latency we need token histograms - small, medium, large buckets. If you can provide a sample of 500 requests representative across both paths that would be ideal 18:03 Mike Chen: we can do that, will sanitize PII and share 500 prompts plus aggregate token histograms 18:10 Alex Reed: great. On SLOs - you mentioned 120-200ms target for auth; is that 95th or median? 18:18 Mike Chen: target is p95 <= 200ms, p99 ideally <= 350ms for auth. For enrichment p95 <= 2s is fine, p99 <= 4s 18:30 Priya Sen: that's helpful. For P95 200ms on auth we'll likely need a low-latency variant - small context, smaller model, and pinned capacity. We'll propose a Dedicated pool with warm KV caches and fixed concurrency slots to hit p95. 18:44 Alex Reed: cost constraints? are you trying to minimize token cost or per-hour reserved capacity? 18:50 Mike Chen: product team wants to keep monthly inference cost under $18k for the POC while meeting latency SLOs. If we need Dedicated it's okay but keep within that envelope for the pilot 19:02 Priya Sen: good to know - we'll produce two sizing options: hosted with autoscaled warm pools vs Dedicated reserved pool; each will show expected monthly cost vs latency targets 19:15 Kayla Park: what about model choices - do you recommend small Llama variants or something else? 19:22 Priya Sen: for short auth decisioning a quantized 7B-class model can deliver sub-200ms p95 on modern GPUs with proper batching disabled for single-token generation; for enrichment a 13B or 33B quantized model gives better quality for longer contexts. We'll propose model family mapping in the sizing doc 19:39 Marco Liu: also we can run a short benchmark against your sample traces — we'll run two configs: (A) latency-focused (single-concurrency warm runs) and (B) throughput-focused (burst QPS with batching/kv caching turned on) and report p50/p95/p99 and throughput 19:58 Alex Reed: timeline - can we aim to get samples by 2025-09-17, Redwood to run bench week of 2025-09-22, results review 2025-09-25? 20:08 Mike Chen: that timeline works for us, 2-3 weeks for initial bench and follow-ups is fine 20:15 Priya Sen: benchmarks we run will include: cold-start latency (scale from zero), warm steady-state p95/p99, throughput @ target p95, and cost-per-1M tokens estimated. We'll also collect trace-level latencies, GPU utilization, and any errors 20:32 Jamal Ortiz: network constraints - we need VPC peering in us-west2 and egress limits; also don't expose customer data to shared logs. How will Redwood handle that? 20:42 Alex Reed: for the pilot we can do Dedicated with VPC peering and private control plane. We'll include SOC2 and network diagram in the security packet. Priya will follow up with the exact network ports and CIDRs 20:54 Laura Diaz: one more: do you support bringing our own KMS? we need keys under our control 21:00 Priya Sen: yes, we have KMS integrations and HSM options for Private deployments; for Dedicated pilot we can enable customer-managed keys - we'll detail in the security doc 21:10 Mike Chen: excellent. Competitors we've talked to included OpenAI (fast api), Anthropic (safety controls), and some in-house GPU hosts; our concern is consistency at scale and predictable costs 21:22 Alex Reed: understood. On benchmarking harness - we'll share a Git repo link (private) with instructions; it will include the runner, tokenization, and scripts to replay traffic. We'll also provide an anonymized result template 21:35 Priya Sen: for modeling concurrency we'll generate synthetic fanout per your described 1.5x multiplier and run a sensitivity sweep across qps 50 -> 500 to show latency curves 21:46 Kayla Park: do you simulate KV-cache hit/miss? enrichment benefits a lot from caching merchant descriptors 21:52 Priya Sen: yes we can simulate cache hit ratios (0%, 50%, 90%) to show cost/latency impact 21:58 Alex Reed: OK to recap next steps: Alex share sizing/pricing spreadsheet; Priya share benchmark harness and propose specific configs; Stratos to provide traces and token histograms; schedule bench and review 21:10 Mike Chen: yes, and we'll confirm internal stakeholders for security review 21:25 Laura Diaz: noted, I'll send names to Alex after this 21:35 Alex Reed: any final outstanding questions? 21:42 Mike Chen: one ask - if Dedicated looks like overkill, can you show a hosted config with reserved warm pods that still gets p95? 21:49 Priya Sen: yes we'll include a hosted warm-pool config and the tradeoffs for cold starts and noisy neighbors 21:55 Alex Reed: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with materials by Monday. Appreciate the details and the example prompts. 21:58 End of call
